The expense increase is not fully explained by the selected rows: a restructuring and other charges line appears only in the event quarter with no baseline comparator, so the split between recurring cost pressure and one-time charges cannot be established from this extract. Revenue direction is mixed by component and segment: card revenues and net interest income rose while cash processing, interchange, consumer services and money movement revenues fell, and B2B services revenue rose. The GAAP net loss narrowed sequentially, but that improvement is driven by a much smaller other expense, net, and by a smaller income tax benefit, not by operating performance; the smaller tax benefit is a reduced offset to the pretax loss, not a reduced tax drag. Segment totals reconcile to GAAP operating revenue through the disclosed reconciliation rows, so the segment view and the GAAP view are consistent in level, but neither identifies a causal driver. All comparisons are sequential displayed-value arithmetic on selected rows, not year-over-year, not non-GAAP, and not guidance. Missing evidence includes the full filings, non-GAAP reconciliations, guidance, revenue and cost drivers, segment profitability, and any baseline restructuring comparator. Because the operating deterioration and the one-time charge cannot be separated on this evidence, the research state is held for review rather than upgraded or invalidated.
